ΠLIST.description: Multiplies together all elements of a list.
ΠLIST.name: List product

Σ.description: Sums an expression over an integer index running from a start value to an end value. Symbolic limits leave the sum as an algebraic.
Σ.name: Summation

Σ+.description: Appends a data point to the statistics matrix ΣDAT, creating it if needed: a real for one-variable data, a vector or several reals for one row, or a matrix for several rows.
Σ+.name: Add data point

Σ-.description: Removes the last data point (row) from ΣDAT and returns it, a real for one-column data or a vector otherwise. Useful for correcting a wrong entry.

ΣLINE.description: Returns the fitted line from ΣPAR as an algebraic in the independent variable, ready for plotting or evaluation.
ΣLINE.name: Regression line

ΣLIST.description: Adds up all elements of a list.
ΣLIST.name: List sum

ΣX.description: Adds up the independent-column entries of ΣDAT.
ΣX.name: Sum of x

ΣX*Y.description: Multiplies each independent value in ΣDAT by its matching dependent value and returns the total.
ΣX*Y.name: Sum of x times y

ΣX2.description: Sums the squared entries of the independent-variable (XCOL) column of the statistics matrix ΣDAT.
ΣX2.name: Sum of x squared

ΣXY.description: Adds up, row by row, the products of the independent and dependent columns of the statistics matrix ΣDAT.
ΣXY.name: Sum of x times y

ΣX^2.description: Squares each independent-column entry of ΣDAT and returns the total.
ΣX^2.name: Sum of x squared

ΣY.description: Adds up the dependent-column entries of ΣDAT.
ΣY.name: Sum of y

ΣY2.description: Sums the squared entries of the dependent-variable (YCOL) column of the statistics matrix ΣDAT.
ΣY2.name: Sum of y squared

ΣY^2.description: Squares each dependent-column entry of ΣDAT and returns the total.
ΣY^2.name: Sum of y squared

π.description: Returns the constant pi, either as the symbol 'π' or, when numeric results or numeric constants are selected, as the 12-digit real 3.14159265359.
π.name: Pi

↑MATCH.description: Rewrites an expression with a pattern and replacement (optionally a condition), matching subexpressions from the innermost outward; & names are wildcards. Returns the result and 1 if anything changed, else 0.
↑MATCH.name: Match and replace, bottom up

→.description: Creates local variables: it takes values from the stack, binds them to the following names, and evaluates the program or algebraic that follows with those names defined.
→.name: Create local variables

→A.description: Returns the memory address of an object as a binary integer; needs library 256 attached.

→A.name: Object address

→ALG.description: Gathers n objects from the stack, with their count in level 1, into an algebraic object without checking that the result is well formed; needs library 256 attached.
→ALG.name: Stack to algebraic

→ARRY.description: Gathers stack objects into an array: with a count it builds a vector, with a list of row and column counts a matrix filled row by row.

→CD.description: Turns a string of hexadecimal digits into a code object containing those nibbles, without running it; needs library 256 attached.
→CD.name: Hex string to code object

→COL.description: Splits a matrix into its columns, pushing each column as a vector followed by the column count. Applied to a vector, it pushes the elements and their count.
→COL.name: Matrix to columns

→DATE.description: Sets the system clock's date from a real number written in the active date format (MM.DDYYYY by default).
→DATE.name: Set date

→DIAG.description: Extracts the main diagonal of a matrix, square or rectangular, as a vector.
→DIAG.name: Matrix diagonal to vector

→FONT.description: Makes a font object the system font used to show the stack and the command line.
→FONT.name: Set system font

→GROB.description: Renders any object as a graphics object in a chosen font size (1 small, 2 medium, 3 large); size 0 draws algebraics the way the EquationWriter shows them.
→GROB.name: To graphics object

→H.description: Converts any object to a string of hexadecimal digits giving its nibbles in memory order; needs library 256 attached.
→H.name: To hex

→HEADER.description: Sets how many lines, from 0 to 2, the status header above the stack occupies.
→HEADER.name: Set header size

→HMS.description: Converts a decimal number of hours (or degrees) to HH.MMSS form.
→HMS.name: Decimal to hours-minutes-seconds

→KEYTIME.description: Sets the keyboard debounce time, the delay in clock ticks the calculator waits before accepting another key press.
→KEYTIME.name: Set key debounce time

→LANGUAGE.description: Chooses the language of system messages by number: 0 for English, 1 for French, 2 for Spanish.
→LANGUAGE.name: Set language

→LCD.description: Shows a graphics object on the screen, placing its top-left corner at the top-left of the display.

→LIST.description: Collects a given count of stack objects into a list, the deepest of them becoming the first element.
→LIST.name: Stack to list

→LST.description: Gathers n objects from the stack, with their count in level 1, into a list; needs library 256 attached.
→LST.name: Stack to list

→MINIFONT.description: Installs a font object as the minifont, the small font used for menu labels and compact display text.
→MINIFONT.name: Set minifont

→NDISP.description: Sets the number of lines the stack display uses for showing objects.
→NDISP.name: Set number of stack lines

→NUM.description: Evaluates an object fully to a number, replacing symbolic constants such as π and e by their numeric values and variables by their contents.
→NUM.name: To number

→PRG.description: Gathers n objects from the stack, with their count in level 1, into a program; needs library 256 attached.
→PRG.name: Stack to program

→Q.description: Turns a real number into the algebraic fraction that best approximates it at the current display precision.
→Q.name: To quotient

→Qπ.description: Approximates a real number as a fraction, or as a fraction times π when that gives a simpler result, and returns it as an algebraic; also works on each number in an expression.
→Qπ.name: To quotient times π

→RAM.description: Replaces an object that lives in ROM, or refers to ROM, by a full copy in RAM; objects already in RAM come back unchanged. Needs library 256 attached.
→RAM.name: Copy to RAM

→ROW.description: Splits a matrix into its rows, pushing each row as a vector followed by the row count. Applied to a vector, it pushes the individual elements and their count.
→ROW.name: Matrix to rows

→S2.description: Disassembles an object into a string of System RPL source that ASM can assemble again. Part of the development library.
→S2.name: To System RPL source

→STR.description: Converts any object to a string showing how it is displayed, using the current number format for reals.
→STR.name: To string

→TAG.description: Attaches a label to an object, producing a tagged object; the tag can be given as a string or a name.
→TAG.name: Stack to tag

→TIME.description: Sets the system clock's time from a real number in 24-hour HH.MMSS form.
→TIME.name: Set time

→UNIT.description: Builds a unit object from a plain number and a unit object, attaching the units of the second to the first; whatever number the unit object carries is ignored. Useful in programs that compute a bare value and then label it.
→UNIT.name: To unit object

→V2.description: Combines two reals into a two-element vector, read as rectangular or polar coordinates according to the current mode; when flag -19 is set it builds a complex number instead.
→V2.name: To 2-element vector

→V3.description: Combines three reals into a three-element vector, interpreting them as rectangular, cylindrical or spherical coordinates according to the current mode.
→V3.name: To 3-element vector

↓MATCH.description: Rewrites an expression with a pattern and replacement (optionally a condition), matching from the whole expression inward; & names are wildcards. Returns the result and 1 if anything changed, else 0.
↓MATCH.name: Match and replace, top down

∂.description: Differentiates an expression by the named variable. The result is symbolic, or a number when the variable already holds a value.
∂.name: Derivative

√.description: Gives the principal square root. A negative real yields a complex result, and units and algebraics are handled as well.
√.name: Square root

∞.description: Puts the symbolic constant for unsigned infinity on the stack, for use in limits, integrals and series.
∞.name: Infinity

∫.description: Integrates an expression over a variable between two limits. It integrates symbolically when it can; with numeric evaluation it integrates numerically, to an accuracy set by the display format.
∫.name: Integral

≠.description: Tests two objects for inequality, returning 1 when they differ and 0 when they are equal; with names or algebraics it builds a symbolic comparison.
≠.name: Not equal

≤.description: Compares level 2 against level 1 and pushes 1 if it is smaller or equal, else 0; accepts reals, binary integers, strings and compatible units, and yields a symbolic comparison for names or algebraics.
≤.name: Less than or equal

≥.description: Compares level 2 against level 1 and pushes 1 if it is larger or equal, else 0; accepts reals, binary integers, strings and compatible units, and yields a symbolic comparison for names or algebraics.
≥.name: Greater than or equal

▶.description: Infix form of storing a value in a variable, as produced by the store key in algebraic mode; the value is kept as the result.
▶.name: Infix store

!.description: Factorial of the value before it. For a value that is not a whole number it gives the gamma function of the value plus one.

%.description: x percent of y: %(x,y) is x times y divided by 100.

%CHANGE.description: How many percent y is above (or below) x: %CHANGE(x,y).

%TOTAL.description: What percentage of x the value y is: %TOTAL(x,y).

*.description: Multiplies two values. A list or matrix times a number scales each element.

+.description: Adds two values. Numbers, complex numbers, lists and matrices all work.

-.description: Subtracts the second value from the first. Works on numbers, complex numbers, lists and matrices.

/.description: Divides the first value by the second.

10ˣ.description: 10 raised to the power of the value.

<.description: 1 when the first value is smaller than the second, else 0.

=.description: Builds an equation from two expressions. It is not a test and stores nothing.

==.description: 1 when both values are equal, else 0. This is the test; = builds an equation.

>.description: 1 when the first value is larger than the second, else 0.

ABS.description: Size of a value without its sign. For a complex number (x,y), its distance from the origin.

ACOS.description: The angle whose cosine is the value, from 0° to 180° (or the same range in radians or grads). Outside −1 to 1 the result is complex.

ACOT.description: The angle whose cotangent is the value.

ACSC.description: The angle whose cosecant is the value.

ADDCOL.description: Inserts a vector as a new column before the given column of a matrix variable: ADDCOL name;vector;column.

ADDROW.description: Inserts a vector as a new row before the given row of a matrix variable: ADDROW name;vector;row.

ALOG.description: 10 to the power of the value, computed more exactly than with ^.

AND.description: 1 when both values are non-zero, else 0.

ARC.description: Draws an arc: ARC x;y;r;from;to draws part of a circle of radius r around (x,y) between two angles.

ARG.description: Angle from the positive real axis to a complex value (x,y), in the current angle mode.

ASEC.description: The angle whose secant is the value.

ASIN.description: The angle whose sine is the value, from −90° to 90° (or the same range in radians or grads). Complex results are possible.

ATAN.description: The angle whose tangent is the value, from −90° to 90° (or the same range in radians or grads).

Ans.description: The result of the last calculation, for use in the next one.

BOX.description: Draws a rectangle from two opposite corners: BOX x1;y1;x2;y2.

BREAK.description: Leaves the loop it is in.

CASE.description: Runs the first of several IF test THEN commands END clauses whose test holds; the whole ends with END.

CEILING.description: The smallest whole number not below the value.

CHECK.description: Ticks function number n in the current aplet's Symbolic view, so it is plotted and tabulated: CHECK n.

CHOOSE.description: Shows a choose box and stores the number of the item picked: CHOOSE variable;title;item1;item2...

COLNORM.description: The largest sum of absolute values found in any column of a matrix.

COMB.description: How many ways there are to pick r of n things when the order does not matter: COMB(n,r).

COND.description: Condition number of a square matrix, based on its column norm.

CONJ.description: Flips the sign of the imaginary part: (3,4) becomes (3,−4).

COS.description: Cosine of an angle in the current angle mode.

DEG→RAD.description: Converts an angle from degrees to radians.

DELCOL.description: Removes a column from a matrix variable: DELCOL name;column.

DELROW.description: Removes a row from a matrix variable: DELROW name;row.

DISP.description: Shows text and values on a line of the display, 1 at the top to 7 at the bottom: DISP line;items.

DISPLAY→.description: Saves the display in a graphic variable (G0 to G9): DISPLAY→ name.

DO.description: Loop that runs at least once: DO commands UNTIL test END.

DO1VSTATS.description: Computes the one-variable statistics of a data set (H1 to H5) into their variables.

DO2VSTATS.description: Computes the two-variable statistics of a data set (S1 to S5) into their variables.

DOT.description: Dot product of two vectors or matrices of the same size.

EDITMAT.description: Opens the matrix editor on a matrix variable; a program goes on when OK is pressed.

EEX.description: Starts the power-of-ten part of a number: 2E3 is 2000.

EIGENVAL.description: The eigenvalues of a square matrix, as a vector.

EIGENVV.description: Eigenvectors and eigenvalues of a square matrix, returned as a list holding two arrays.

ELSE.description: Starts the commands an IF runs when its test fails.

END.description: Ends a branch or loop: IF, CASE, IFERR, FOR, DO and WHILE.

EXP.description: e to the power of the value, computed more exactly than with ^.

EXPM1.description: e to the power of the value, minus 1. Keeps its precision for values close to zero.

FLOOR.description: The largest whole number not above the value.

FNROOT.description: Searches for a value of the variable that makes the expression zero, starting from a guess: FNROOT(expression,variable,guess).

FOR.description: Counted loop: FOR variable=start TO end [STEP increment]; commands END.

FRAC.description: The part of the value after the decimal point.

FREEZE.description: Keeps what a program drew on the display until a key is pressed.

GETKEY.description: Waits for a key and stores its code (row, column and shift plane) in a variable.

GROBNOT.description: Inverts every dot of a graphic variable.

GROBOR.description: Lays one graphic over another with logical OR, its top left corner at a position: GROBOR name1;(x,y);name2.

GROBXOR.description: Lays one graphic over another with logical XOR, its top left corner at a position: GROBXOR name1;(x,y);name2.

HMS→.description: Converts a time or angle written H.MMSS to decimal hours or degrees.

IDENMAT.description: A square matrix of the given size with ones on the diagonal and zeros elsewhere.

IF.description: Starts a branch: IF test THEN commands [ELSE commands] END.

IFERR.description: Runs the commands after THEN when the commands before it cause an error, instead of stopping the program.

IFTE.description: The second argument when the test is non-zero, else the third: IFTE(test,true,false).

IM.description: Imaginary part: y of the complex value (x,y).

INPUT.description: Shows an input form with one field and stores what is entered: INPUT variable;title;label;help;default.

INT.description: The value with its fractional part dropped.

INVERSE.description: Inverse of a square matrix; complex matrices work too.

ISOLATE.description: Solves expression=0 for the first occurrence of a variable. Formal names s1 and n1 in the result stand for any sign and any integer.

ITERATE.description: Evaluates an expression again and again, each time with the last result as the variable's new value: ITERATE(expression,variable,start,times).

LINE.description: Draws a line between two points: LINE x1;y1;x2;y2.

LINEAR?.description: 1 when the expression is linear in the variable, else 0.

LN.description: Logarithm to base e. Complex arguments work.

LNP1.description: Natural logarithm of the value plus 1. Keeps its precision for values close to zero.

LQ.description: Splits a matrix into a lower trapezoidal, an orthogonal and a permutation matrix, returned as a list.

LSQ.description: The minimum-norm least-squares solution of a system given by two matrices.

LU.description: Splits a square matrix into a lower triangular, an upper triangular and a permutation matrix, returned as a list.

MAKEGROB.description: Builds a graphic from a width, a height and hexadecimal data: MAKEGROB name;width;height;hex.

MAKELIST.description: Builds a list by evaluating an expression as a variable steps from a start to an end value: MAKELIST(expression,variable,start,end,step).

MAKEMAT.description: Builds a matrix of the given rows and columns from an expression; I and J in it stand for the row and the column: MAKEMAT(expression,rows,columns).

MANT.description: The significant digits of a value, without its power of ten.

MAXREAL.description: The largest real number the calculator holds, 9.99999999999E499.

MINREAL.description: The smallest positive real number the calculator holds, 1E−499.

MOD.description: Remainder of the value before MOD divided by the value after it.

MSGBOX.description: Shows text and values in a box until OK is pressed.

NEG.description: Changes the sign of the value after it. Complex numbers work.

NOT.description: 1 when the value is zero, else 0.

NTHROOT.description: Root of a given degree: the degree goes before NTHROOT, the value after it.

OR.description: 1 when either value is non-zero, else 0.

PERM.description: How many ways there are to pick r of n things in order: PERM(n,r).

PIXOFF.description: Turns off the dot at a point: PIXOFF x;y.

PIXON.description: Turns on the dot at a point: PIXON x;y.

PLOT→.description: Saves the Plot view as a graphic: PLOT→ name.

POLYCOEF.description: The coefficients of the polynomial that has the given roots.

POLYEVAL.description: Value of a polynomial, given by its coefficients, at a point.

POLYFORM.description: Rewrites an expression as a polynomial in the given variable.

POLYROOT.description: The roots of a polynomial given by its coefficients.

POS.description: Where an element first occurs in a list, or 0 when it is not there.

PRDISPLAY.description: Prints the display on an infrared printer.

PREDX.description: The x value the current fit of the Statistics aplet gives for a y value.

PREDY.description: The y value the current fit of the Statistics aplet gives for an x value.

PRHISTORY.description: Prints everything in HOME's history on an infrared printer.

PRVAR.description: Prints a variable's name and contents; PRVAR name;PROG or name;NOTE prints a program or a note.

QR.description: Splits a matrix into an orthogonal, an upper trapezoidal and a permutation matrix, returned as a list.

QUAD.description: Solves a quadratic expression=0 for a variable; the formal name s1 in the result stands for either sign.

QUOTE.description: Keeps an expression from being evaluated, so that it is stored as written.

RAD→DEG.description: Converts an angle from radians to degrees.

RANDMAT.description: Fills a matrix variable (M0 to M9) with random whole numbers between −9 and 9: RANDMAT M;rows;cols.

RANDOM.description: A random number between 0 and 1. RANDSEED sets where the sequence starts.

RANDSEED.description: Sets the starting point of RANDOM's sequence.

RE.description: Real part: x of the complex value (x,y).

RECURSE.description: Defines a sequence by a recurrence, usually stored into a function such as U1(N): RECURSE(name,term-n,term1,term2).

REDIM.description: Changes the size of a matrix or vector variable; the size is a list {rows,columns} or {n}.

REPEAT.description: Starts the commands of a WHILE loop.

REPLACE.description: Overwrites part of a graphic, list or matrix with another one, from a start position: REPLACE name;start;object.

REVERSE.description: The list with its elements in reverse order.

ROUND.description: Rounds a value to the given number of decimal places; a negative count rounds to that many significant digits.

ROWNORM.description: The largest sum of absolute values found in any row of a matrix.

RREF.description: The matrix in reduced row echelon form, as used to solve a system of linear equations.

RUN.description: Runs a program by its name: RUN name, in quotes when it has spaces.

SCALE.description: Multiplies one row of a matrix variable by a value: SCALE name;value;row.

SCALEADD.description: Adds value times row r1 of a matrix variable to its row r2: SCALEADD M;value;r1;r2.

SCHUR.description: Schur decomposition of a square matrix: a list of two matrices, orthogonal (or unitary) and upper triangular.

SELECT.description: Makes the named aplet the current one: SELECT name. Put a name with spaces in quotes.

SETDEPEND.description: Sets the column of a two-variable data set's dependent values.

SETFREQ.description: Sets where a one-variable data set takes its frequencies from: a column or a number.

SETINDEP.description: Sets the column of a two-variable data set's independent values.

SETSAMPLE.description: Sets the column a one-variable data set takes its values from.

SETVIEWS.description: Replaces the current aplet's VIEWS menu with entries given as trios of prompt, program name and view number, separated by semicolons.

SIGN.description: 1 for a positive value, −1 for a negative one, 0 for zero. For a complex number, the unit vector in its direction.

SIN.description: Sine of an angle in the current angle mode (Degrees, Radians or Grads).

SIZE.description: How many elements a list has. For a matrix, its rows and columns as a list.

SORT.description: The list sorted in ascending order.

SPECRAD.description: Largest absolute value among the eigenvalues of a square matrix (its spectral radius).

STEP.description: Gives the increment of a FOR loop; without it the step is 1.

STO▶.description: Stores the value on its left in the variable named on its right.

SUB.description: Copies part of a graphic, list or matrix, from a start to an end position, into a variable: SUB name;object;start;end.

SVD.description: Splits a matrix into two square orthogonal matrices and a vector of singular values, returned as a list.

SVL.description: The singular values of a matrix, as a vector.

SWAPCOL.description: Exchanges two columns of a matrix variable.

SWAPROW.description: Exchanges two rows of a matrix variable.

TAN.description: Tangent of an angle in the current angle mode.

TAYLOR.description: Taylor polynomial of an expression in a variable around 0, to the order given: TAYLOR(expression,variable,order).

THEN.description: Starts the commands an IF, IFERR or CASE branch runs when its test holds.

TLINE.description: Inverts every dot along a line, so drawing the same line twice removes it: TLINE x1;y1;x2;y2.

TO.description: Gives the end value of a FOR loop.

TRACE.description: Sum of the diagonal elements of a square matrix.

TRN.description: Swaps the rows and columns of a matrix. A complex matrix is also conjugated.

TRUNCATE.description: Cuts a value off after the given number of decimal places.

UNCHECK.description: Clears the tick of function number n in the current aplet: UNCHECK n.

UNTIL.description: Gives the test that ends a DO loop.

UTPC.description: Probability that a chi-squared variable with the given degrees of freedom is larger than the value: UTPC(degrees,value).

UTPF.description: Probability that a Snedecor F variable with the given numerator and denominator degrees of freedom is larger than the value.

UTPN.description: Probability that a normal variable with the given mean and variance is larger than the value: UTPN(mean,variance,value).

UTPT.description: Probability that a Student's t variable with the given degrees of freedom is larger than the value.

WAIT.description: Pauses a program for a number of seconds.

WHILE.description: Loop that runs while a test holds: WHILE test REPEAT commands END.

XOR.description: 1 when exactly one of the two values is non-zero, else 0.

XPON.description: The power of ten of a value.

ZEROGROB.description: Creates an empty graphic of a width and height: ZEROGROB name;width;height.

eˣ.description: e raised to the power of the value. Complex arguments work.

x⁻¹.description: One divided by the value. For a square matrix, its inverse.

ΠLIST.description: Multiplies all elements of a list.

ΣLIST.description: Adds all elements of a list.

UTPF.description: Probability that a Snedecor F variable with the given numerator and denominator degrees of freedom is larger than the value.

UTPN.description: Probability that a normal variable with the given mean and variance is larger than the value: UTPN(mean,variance,value).

UTPT.description: Probability that a Student's t variable with the given degrees of freedom is larger than the value.

WAIT.description: Pauses a program for a number of seconds.

WHILE.description: Loop that runs while a test holds: WHILE test REPEAT commands END.

XOR.description: 1 when exactly one of the two values is non-zero, else 0.

XPON.description: The power of ten of a value.

ZEROGROB.description: Creates an empty graphic of a width and height: ZEROGROB name;width;height.

^.description: Raises the value before it to the power after it.

eˣ.description: e raised to the power of the value. Complex arguments work.

x⁻¹.description: One divided by the value. For a square matrix, its inverse.

|.description: Evaluates the expression before it with variables set to the values given after it: expression|(X=3).

ΔLIST.description: A list of the differences between neighbouring elements, one element shorter than the list.

ΠLIST.description: Multiplies all elements of a list.

Σ.description: Sum of an expression as a variable runs from a start value to an end value: Σ(variable=start,end,expression).

ΣLIST.description: Adds all elements of a list.

→DISPLAY.description: Shows a graphic variable on the display: →DISPLAY name.

→GROB.description: Draws an expression as a graphic in font size 1, 2 or 3 and stores it: →GROB name;expression;size.

→HMS.description: Converts decimal hours or degrees to the H.MMSS form.

→PLOT.description: Puts a graphic into the Plot view: →PLOT name.

∂.description: Differentiates an expression: ∂ is followed by the variable and the expression in brackets. Use a formal name (s1 to s5) to get a symbolic result.

√.description: Square root of the value after it. Negative and complex values give complex roots.

∫.description: Integrates an expression between two limits: ∫(lower,upper,expression,variable). With a formal name (s1 to s5) as a limit the result is symbolic.

≤.description: 1 when the first value is not larger than the second, else 0.

≥.description: 1 when the first value is not smaller than the second, else 0.

%.description: x percent of y; y stays.

%CH.description: The change from y to x as a percentage of y.

+/-.description: Changes the sign of x, or of the exponent being typed.

ABS.description: The absolute value of x: x without its sign; the length of a complex number.

ACOS.description: The arc cosine of x, in the current angle mode.

ACOSH.description: The inverse hyperbolic cosine of x.

ADV.description: Feeds the printer paper by one line.

AGRAPH.description: Draws the Alpha register as dot columns on the display: each character is one column of eight dots, placed at the row in y and the column in x.

AIP.description: Appends x's integer part to the Alpha register.

ALENG.description: How many characters the Alpha register holds.

ALL.description: Shows numbers with all their digits (ALL display format).

ALLΣ.description: Statistics with all 13 summation registers, which every curve fit needs.

ALPHA.description: Opens the ALPHA menu, for typing letters into the Alpha register or a name.

AND.description: The bitwise AND of y and x, as 36-bit integers.

AON.description: Turns Alpha mode on, showing the Alpha register with the ALPHA menu.

ARCL.description: Appends a register's or variable's contents to the Alpha register; numbers in the current display format. Its key in Alpha mode is RCL.

AROT.description: Rotates the Alpha register by x characters, to the left for positive x.

ASHF.description: Drops the six leftmost characters of the Alpha register.

ASIN.description: The arc sine of x, in the current angle mode.

ASINH.description: The inverse hyperbolic sine of x.

ASSIGN.description: Puts a function, a program or a variable on a key of the CUSTOM menu.

ASTO.description: Stores the Alpha register's first six characters in a register or variable. Its key in Alpha mode is STO.

ATAN.description: The arc tangent of x, in the current angle mode.

ATANH.description: The inverse hyperbolic tangent of x.

ATOX.description: Removes the leftmost character of the Alpha register and returns its character code.

AVIEW.description: Shows the Alpha register on the display.

BASE.description: Opens the BASE menu: hexadecimal, decimal, octal and binary integers and their logic.

BASE+.description: Adds y and x as 36-bit integers. The + key in the BASE menu.

BASE+/-.description: Changes the sign of x as a 36-bit two's complement integer. The +/- key in the BASE menu.

BASE-.description: Subtracts x from y as 36-bit integers. The − key in the BASE menu.

BASE×.description: Multiplies y by x as 36-bit integers. The × key in the BASE menu.

BASE÷.description: Divides y by x as 36-bit integers, dropping the remainder. The ÷ key in the BASE menu.

BEEP.description: Plays a short tune of four tones.

BEST.description: Picks the curve-fit model that fits the statistics data best.

BINM.description: Binary mode: shows integers in base 2.

BIT?.description: Tests bit x of y. A program runs its next line only if the bit is set.

BST.description: Moves the program pointer back one line. With no menu shown, the ▲ key does it.

CATALOG.description: Opens the CATALOG menu: functions, programs, and the real, complex and matrix variables.

CLALL.description: Clears all programs and data, after asking. It cannot be undone.

CLD.description: Removes the message shown on the display.

CLKEYS.description: Removes every assignment from the CUSTOM menu.

CLMENU.description: Removes every key definition of the programmable menu.

CLRG.description: Sets every numbered storage register to zero.

CLST.description: Sets the four stack registers X, Y, Z and T to zero.

CLX.description: Sets x to zero. The ⬅ key does it too when no number is being typed.

CLΣ.description: Clears the statistics data in the summation registers.

COMB.description: The number of ways to choose x items from y, ignoring order.

COMPLEX.description: Joins y and x into the complex number y + ix, or splits a complex x into its two parts (also for matrices).
COMPLEX.stack: y x → y+ix; z → re im

CONVERT.description: Opens the CONVERT menu: angle and time conversions, polar and rectangular coordinates, number parts.

CORR.description: The correlation coefficient of the statistics data for the current curve-fit model.

COS.description: The cosine of x, in the current angle mode.

CPX?.description: Tests whether x is a complex number. A program runs its next line only if so.

CPXRES.description: Lets functions return complex results from real arguments (the square root of −1 gives i).

CROSS.description: Cross product of y and x, two vectors (matrices or complex numbers).

CUSTOM.description: Opens the CUSTOM menu, the keys you assigned.

DECM.description: Decimal mode for the BASE menu: shows integers in base 10.

DEL.description: Deletes a number of lines from the current program, in program entry.

DELAY.description: Sets the printer's delay after each line to x seconds.

DELR.description: Deletes the current row of the matrix open in the editor or indexed.

DET.description: The determinant of the square matrix in x.

DIM.description: Makes a named matrix y rows by x columns, creating it if needed.

DIM?.description: The number of rows and columns of the matrix in x.

DISP.description: Opens the DISP menu: display formats and the radix mark.

DOT.description: Dot product of y and x, two vectors (matrices or complex numbers).

DSE.description: Takes the step from a loop counter ccccccc.fffii in a register or variable; in a program the next line is skipped once the counter is at or below fff.
DSE.long: Decrement, skip if less or equal

E.description: Starts the exponent of the number being typed: 3 E 4 is 3×10⁴.

EDIT.description: Opens the matrix in x in the matrix editor.

EDITN.description: Opens a named matrix in the matrix editor.

END.description: Ends a program. Every program ends with one.

ENG.description: Engineering notation with a number of digits: exponents in multiples of three.

ENTER.description: Ends number entry and copies x into y; the stack lifts and t is lost.

EXIT.description: Leaves the current menu, or stops what is being typed or prompted.

E↑X.description: The natural exponential: e to the power x.

E↑X-1.description: eˣ − 1, accurate for x close to zero.

FC?.description: Tests whether a flag is clear. A program runs its next line only if so.

FC?C.description: Tests whether a flag is clear, then clears it. In a program, the next line runs only if it was clear. Flags 00-35 and 81-99 only.

FCSTX.description: The x value the current curve fit gives for the y in x.

FCSTY.description: The y value the current curve fit gives for the x in x.

FIX.description: Fixed notation with a number of digits after the point.

FLAGS.description: Opens the FLAGS menu: setting, clearing and testing flags.

FNRM.description: Frobenius norm of x, a matrix: the square root of all its elements squared and added up.

FS?.description: Tests whether a flag is set. A program runs its next line only if so.

FS?C.description: Tests whether a flag is set, then clears it. In a program, the next line runs only if it was set. Flags 00-35 and 81-99 only.

GAMMA.description: The gamma function of x; for a positive integer n, Γ(n) is (n−1)!.

GETKEY.description: Waits for a key and returns its number: 1-37 for the keys, 38-74 for the shifted ones.

GETM.description: Copies a part of the indexed matrix, y rows by x columns from the current element, into x.

GRAD.description: Grads angle mode (400 to the circle).

GROW.description: Grow mode for the matrix editor: moving past the last element adds a row.

GTO.description: Goes to a label: from the keyboard it moves the program pointer, in a program it branches.

GTO ..description: Goes to a line number or a global label in program memory, without running anything. Not programmable.

GTO ...description: Goes to a new, empty program space after the last program, ready for a new one. Not programmable.

HEXM.description: Hexadecimal mode: shows integers in base 16.

HMS+.description: Adds y and x, both in hours-minutes-seconds form (H.MMSSss).

HMS-.description: Subtracts x from y, both in hours-minutes-seconds form (H.MMSSss).

I+.description: Moves the row pointer of the indexed matrix down one row.

I-.description: Moves the row pointer of the indexed matrix up one row.

INDEX.description: Makes a named matrix the indexed matrix, for the element and row functions.

INPUT.description: In a program: shows a register or variable with its value and stops, so you can change it; R/S stores x and goes on.

INSR.description: Inserts a row into the indexed matrix.

INTEG.description: Integrates the chosen program with respect to a variable.

INVRT.description: The inverse of the square matrix in x.

ISG.description: Adds the step to a loop counter ccccccc.fffii in a register or variable; in a program the next line is skipped once the counter is above fff.

J+.description: Moves the column pointer of the indexed matrix right one column.

J-.description: Moves the column pointer of the indexed matrix left one column.

KEYASN.description: CUSTOM menu shows your key assignments (the other choice is LCLBL).

KEYG.description: In a program: makes a menu key branch to a label (for the programmable menu).

KEYX.description: In a program: makes a menu key run a label as a subroutine (for the programmable menu).

LASTX.description: Recalls the x a function last used.

LBL.description: Puts a label in a program, for running it and branching to it.

LCLBL.description: CUSTOM menu shows the local labels A-J and a-e of the current program.

LINF.description: Linear curve-fit model: y = m·x + b.

LINΣ.description: Statistics with the six summation registers of a linear fit only.

LIST.description: Prints a number of lines of the current program. Not programmable.

LN1+X.description: ln(1 + x), accurate for x close to zero.

LOGF.description: Logarithmic curve-fit model: y = b + m·ln x.

MAN.description: Manual print mode: the printer prints only what you ask for.

MAT?.description: Tests whether x is a matrix. A program runs its next line only if so.

MEAN.description: The means of the x values and of the y values of the statistics data.

MENU.description: In a program: shows the programmable menu, whose keys KEYG and KEYX define.

MOD.description: The remainder of y divided by x.

MODES.description: Opens the MODES menu: angle and coordinate modes, complex results, register count, beeper.

MVAR.description: In a program: declares a variable for the Solver's or the integrator's variable menu.

NEWMAT.description: Creates a matrix of y rows and x columns, all zeros.

NORM.description: Normal print mode: the printer records the keys you press.

NOT.description: The bitwise NOT of x, as a 36-bit integer.

OCTM.description: Octal mode: shows integers in base 8.

OFF.description: Turns the calculator off. The shifted key does it from the keyboard; XEQ "OFF" is the form a program uses.

OLD.description: Recalls the current element of the indexed matrix (as RCLEL does).

ON.description: Keeps the calculator on: it no longer turns itself off after ten minutes.

OR.description: The bitwise OR of y and x, as 36-bit integers.

PERM.description: The number of ordered arrangements of x items taken from y.

PGM.FCN.description: Opens the PGM.FCN menu: programming functions.

PIXEL.description: Turns on the display dot at row y and column x.

POLAR.description: Polar coordinate mode: complex numbers show as a length and an angle.

POSA.description: Searches the Alpha register for x (a character code or a string) and returns its position, or −1.

PRGM.description: Turns program entry on or off.

PROB.description: Opens the PROB menu: combinations, permutations, factorial, gamma, random numbers.

PROMPT.description: In a program: shows the Alpha register and stops.

PRP.description: Prints a program, the current one if no label is given. Not programmable.

PRSTK.description: Prints X, Y, Z and T, the stack registers.

PRUSR.description: Prints the user variables and programs.

PSE.description: In a program: pauses for about a second.

PUTM.description: Stores the matrix in x into the indexed matrix, from its current element.

QUIET.description: Turns the beeper off or on (flag 26). Not programmable.

R/S.description: Runs the program from the current line, or stops a running one. In program entry it puts a STOP into the program.

R<>R.description: Swaps rows y and x of the indexed matrix.

RAN.description: A random number from 0 to just under 1.

RCL.description: Recalls a register or variable into x.

RCL+.description: Recalls a register or variable and adds it to x.

RCL-.description: Recalls a register or variable and subtracts it from x.

RCLEL.description: Recalls the current element of the indexed matrix.

RCLIJ.description: Recalls I and J, the row and column pointers of the indexed matrix.

RCL×.description: Recalls a register or variable and multiplies x by it.

RCL÷.description: Recalls a register or variable and divides x by it.

RDX,.description: Uses a comma as the decimal mark.

RDX..description: Uses a point as the decimal mark.

REAL?.description: Tests whether x is a real number. A program runs its next line only if so.

REALRES.description: Real results only: a real argument that would give a complex result is an error.

RECT.description: Rectangular coordinate mode: complex numbers show as real and imaginary parts.

RND.description: Rounds x to the digits the display format shows.

RNRM.description: Row norm of x, a matrix: the largest sum of absolute values in one of its rows.

ROTXY.description: Rotates y, a 36-bit integer, by x bits: right for positive x, left for negative.

RSUM.description: Sums each row of x, a matrix, giving a column matrix of the sums.

RTN.description: Return: in a program it goes back to the line after the XEQ that called; from the keyboard it sets the program pointer to the program's top.

R↑.description: Rolls the stack up: x goes to y, y to z, z to t, t to x.
R↑.stack: t z y x → z y x t

R↓.description: Rolls the stack down: t goes to z, z to y, y to x, x to t.
R↓.stack: t z y x → x t z y

SCI.description: Scientific notation with a number of digits after the point.

SDEV.description: The standard deviations of the x values and of the y values of the statistics data.

SEED.description: Starts the random number generator from x.

SHOW.description: Shows x with all its digits, the whole Alpha register, or a whole program line, while the key is held.

SIGN.description: 1 for positive x and zero, −1 for negative x, 0 for anything not a number; for a complex x, the unit vector.

SIMQ.description: Sets up the matrix editor for solving a system of linear equations with a number of unknowns.

SIN.description: The sine of x, in the current angle mode.

SIZE.description: Sets the number of numbered storage registers.

SLOPE.description: The slope of the current curve fit to the statistics data.

SOLVE.description: Solves the chosen program for an unknown variable.

SOLVER.description: Opens the SOLVER menu, for finding a value that makes a program's equation zero.

SST.description: Moves the program pointer forward one line, running that line outside program entry. With no menu shown, the ▼ key does it.

STAT.description: Opens the STAT menu: statistics and curve fitting.

STO.description: Stores a copy of x in a register or variable.

STO+.description: Adds x to a register or variable.

STO-.description: Subtracts x from a register or variable.

STOEL.description: Stores x into the current element of the indexed matrix.

STOIJ.description: Moves the indexed matrix's pointers to row y and column x.

STOP.description: Stops a program. In program entry the R/S key puts it into the program.

STO×.description: Multiplies a register or variable by x.

STO÷.description: Divides a register or variable by x.

STR?.description: Tests whether x holds an Alpha string. A program runs its next line only if so.

SUM.description: The sums of the x values and of the y values of the statistics data.

TAN.description: The tangent of x, in the current angle mode.

TONE.description: Plays one of ten tones, 0 to 9.

TOP.FCN.description: Opens the TOP.FCN menu: the functions of the top row of keys, for when another menu covers them.

TRACE.description: Trace print mode: the printer records the keys you press and the results.

UVEC.description: The unit vector in the direction of the matrix or complex number in x.

VARMENU.description: Builds a variable menu from the MVAR lines that follow a global label.

VIEW.description: Shows a register's or variable's contents.

WMEAN.description: The mean of the x values weighted by the y values.

WRAP.description: Wrap mode for the matrix editor: moving past the last element goes back to the first; the matrix does not grow.

X<0?.description: Tests whether x < 0. A program runs its next line only if so.

X<>.description: Swaps x with a register or variable.

X<Y?.description: Tests whether x < y. A program runs its next line only if so.

X=0?.description: Tests whether x = 0. A program runs its next line only if so.

X=Y?.description: Tests whether x = y. A program runs its next line only if so.

X>0?.description: Tests whether x > 0. A program runs its next line only if so.

X>Y?.description: Tests whether x > y. A program runs its next line only if so.

XEQ.description: Runs a function or a program by its name or label.

XOR.description: The bitwise exclusive OR of y and x, as 36-bit integers.

XTOA.description: Appends the character with code x to the Alpha register; a string in x is appended whole.

X≠0?.description: Tests whether x ≠ 0. A program runs its next line only if so.

X≠Y?.description: Tests whether x ≠ y. A program runs its next line only if so.

X≤0?.description: Tests whether x ≤ 0. A program runs its next line only if so.

X≤Y?.description: Tests whether x ≤ y. A program runs its next line only if so.

X≥0?.description: Tests whether x ≥ 0. A program runs its next line only if so.

X≥Y?.description: Tests whether x ≥ y. A program runs its next line only if so.

YINT.description: The y-intercept of the current curve fit to the statistics data.

Σ+.description: Adds the pair y, x to the statistics data in the summation registers; x shows the count.

Σ-.description: Takes the pair y, x out of the statistics data, to correct an entry.

ΣREG.description: Sets the first of the summation registers, which hold the statistics data.

ΣREG?.description: Which register the summation registers start at.

←.description: In the matrix editor: moves one element left.

↑.description: In the matrix editor: moves one element up.

→.description: In the matrix editor: moves one element right.

→DEC.description: Reads x as an octal number and gives its decimal value (for HP-41 programs; not the BASE menu).

→DEG.description: Converts an angle from radians to degrees.

→HMS.description: Converts decimal hours to hours-minutes-seconds form (H.MMSSss).

→OCT.description: Gives the octal digits of a decimal x, as a decimal-looking number (for HP-41 programs; not the BASE menu).

→POL.description: Converts x and y to polar form: the length r in x, the angle θ in y. A complex x is converted in place.

→RAD.description: Converts an angle from degrees to radians.

→REC.description: Converts polar form, the length r in x and the angle θ in y, to rectangular x and y. A complex x is converted in place.

↓.description: In the matrix editor: moves one element down.

∫f(x).description: Opens the integration menu, for integrating a program's function.

⬅.description: Deletes the last character typed; with nothing being typed it clears x. In program entry it deletes the current line.
